shouldFix.title: Every one of the four slice-1 platform profiles omits a component of the four-part profile key the same object declares — and the artifact demonstrates the deferral idiom on a sibling component while leaving this one silently absent
shouldFix.location: /platformProfile/slice1Profiles[0..3] against /platformProfile/key — both on the v2 roster, both new content introduced by this successor
shouldFix.subjectQuote: key: ['osFamily', 'supportedVersionOrBuildSelector', 'architecture', 'filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution'] … relationToEveryTcbEntry: 'Every TCB allowlist entry is keyed by exactly one platformProfile. An entry without a profile key is a failed successor.' … slice1Profiles: {osFamily: 'macos', architecture: 'arm64', filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution: 'apfs-or-hfs-plus-as-declared-at-qualification'}

measurement.theOmissionIsTotalAndExact: I tested every profile against the declared key programmatically. All 4 of 4 slice-1 profiles carry osFamily, architecture and filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution, and all 4 of 4 omit supportedVersionOrBuildSelector. Not one instantiates it.
measurement.theTokenAppearsExactlyOnceInTheEntireArt: 'supportedVersionOrBuildSelector' occurs exactly ONCE in all 13535 bytes — in the key list itself. It appears in no profile, no reservation, no deferral, no routing statement, and no review-guidance line. Nothing anywhere in the document says who supplies it, when, or under whose authority.
measurement.theArtifactKnowsHowToMarkADeferralAndDid: This is what makes it a defect rather than a considered reservation. filesystemWhereItAffectsResolution — a peer component of the same key, in the same objects — carries its deferral inside its value: 'apfs-or-hfs-plus-as-declared-at-qualification' and 'ext4-or-xfs-as-declared-at-qualification'. The drafter had the idiom in hand, applied it to one key component, and left the other simply missing.
measurement.itIsNotCoveredByTheArtifactsOwnReservati: memberPopulation reserves 'Per-OS concrete MEMBERS' to G22. A profile key value is not a member — it is the key members are filed under. And prequalificationAuthorshipBoundary affirmatively claims the key as this contract's own work: 'This contract authors the profile key and identity/resolution predicate.' The artifact claims authorship of the key, so the key's own instances are in scope here, not deferred.
measurement.itIsNotCoveredByAnExternalOwnerEither: I checked the obvious candidate and it does not cover this. COORDINATOR-DECISIONS line 735 routes 'The EXACT machine identifiers, OS versions and cache-state protocol' to the G03/G04 harness-naming — but that pins the RUNNER class for D-006's performance measurements, not the range of OS versions a TCB allowlist entry is valid across. Those are different quantities with different owners, and the second is DR-126/G22's.
measurement.whatItCostsInPractice: As written, macOS 14 and macOS 15 on arm64 are the SAME profile. Their system libc, ICU data and certificate-store contents genuinely differ. So a single allowlist entry keyed to 'macos/arm64' spans both, and an object whose identity changed across that OS boundary satisfies its entry — which is exactly the condition NT-TCB-3 ('A declared-name object whose identityEvidence drifted refuses') exists to refuse. The key component that would discriminate it is declared and then never carried.

shouldFix.whyShouldFixAndNotBlocker: The normative rule survives intact and governs. /platformProfile/key is a four-component key, stated unconditionally, and relationToEveryTcbEntry binds every allowlist entry to a profile with 'An entry without a profile key is a failed successor.' A conforming successor must therefore supply all four components, and where a normative rule and an illustrative instance conflict, the rule wins. So the B1 repair's core — an allowlist that cannot exist without a profile key — is genuinely built and I could not break it. Nothing is orphaned to another row and no authority is exported. This is the artifact's own enumeration failing to conform to the artifact's own rule, not a hole in the rule.
shouldFix.whyItIsNotMerelyAdvisory: Three reasons. First, it sits on the single path this successor exists to create — slice1Profiles is new content on the roster, not inherited noise. Second, slice1Profiles is precisely the object a G22 population packet will copy as its starting point: it is labelled as the slice-1 profiles, it matches /platforms/slice1 exactly on all four entries, and it is the only worked example in the document. A populator following it produces entries that under-discriminate OS versions while appearing to conform. Third, the artifact states the strictest possible consequence for this class of error in its own words — 'An entry without a profile key is a failed successor' — and then ships four instances that do not carry the full key. A contract whose own examples fail its own admission rule invites the next author to treat the rule as decorative.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: One of two, both small and neither requiring a decision this row cannot make. Either (a) carry the sibling idiom across: add supportedVersionOrBuildSelector to each of the four profiles with an explicit deferral value in the same style, e.g. 'as-declared-at-qualification'; or (b) if the component is deliberately not instantiable at contract time, say so once in prequalificationAuthorshipBoundary — one clause naming supportedVersionOrBuildSelector as populated at qualification alongside members, and naming its owner. Option (a) is closer to what the object already does and needs no new ownership statement.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the subject moved. It did not — c404bb8f… at dispatch, at start and at end, 13535 bytes, mode 0444, and I never wrote to it. I re-measured after discovering the repo had advanced, precisely because that is when a subject would move; it had not.

The dispatch's attack 1, an allowlist with no platformProfile key. REFUTED as to the rule, which is what the attack names. /platformProfile/key exists with four components, and relationToEveryTcbEntry binds it unconditionally to every entry: 'Every TCB allowlist entry is keyed by exactly one platformProfile. An entry without a profile key is a failed successor.' There is no unkeyed path. The attack does land one level down, on the artifact's own four instances of that key — see S-1, which is an instance defect, not a missing rule.

The dispatch's attack 2, identity that is still name plus unconstrained version-or-digest. REFUTED, and refuted twice over in the artifact's own bytes. namespacesAndSelectors requires 'the selector the platform uses to name that object (not an unconstrained version-or-digest string)', and resolvedObjectOrPlatformAuthenticatedBuild adds 'Unconstrained version strings are not sufficient.' v1's alternation is gone entirely. digestWhereBytesMustBeBound handles byte collections by requiring that a named algorithm EXIST without picking one — the correct move, since picking would be population-time fiat. architecture closes the cross-arch aliasing case: 'A same name on another architecture is a different member.' I also checked whether the version string re-entered through the back door at platformProfile.key's supportedVersionOrBuildSelector; it did not, because that keys a profile, not a member identity.

The dispatch's attack 3, a missing declared-versus-ambient predicate. REFUTED. resolutionPredicate is ordered, four steps, and closes with a universal: 'Every other source or route is ambient/alternate and MUST refuse.' declaredVersusAmbient defines both sides positively. There is no default-allow branch.

That the resolution predicate has an undefined-state hole when no qualified profile is active — my own attack on step 1, which presupposes an active profile exists. REFUTED, and it fails closed by construction rather than by luck: since every allowlist entry is keyed to exactly one profile, no active profile means no active entries, so nothing can satisfy step 3's 'exact allowlist match', and step 4's universal refuses everything. Running on an unqualified platform therefore refuses rather than silently permitting. The predicate is total.

The dispatch's attack 4, traces that cannot prove full closure. REFUTED on all four escape routes I could construct. Late loading is covered ('late loads after start'), spawned helpers are covered ('descendants and helper tools the core spawns'), non-loader system-class access is covered ('non-loader system-class accesses (cert/font/ICU-class) covered by the taxonomy'), and the initial image is covered. The join is what makes it provable rather than merely observed: 'Every observed event MUST match the signed active-profile table or fail. Partial traces are a failed qualification.' That last sentence is the one that shuts the real hole — an incomplete trace cannot pass by being incomplete.

That observing descendants and helper tools re-owns DR-G07's spawn binding — the strongest over-reach attack available against the B4 repair. REFUTED on the distinction and confirmed against the register. DR-G07 owns whether verification BINDS to spawn (file 04 L154-155, 'descriptor/identity/open-handle or digest recheck that binds verification to spawn'); v2 observes what a spawned process RESOLVES, which is a TCB-closure question. Affirmatively, file 08 line 356 puts 'tool resolution' inside DR-G22's own evidence column — 'negative undeclared libc/framework/cert/font/ICU/tool resolution' — so helper tools are this row's business by the register's own text, not an annexation. surroundingLaw is byte-unchanged and still routes extraction/symlink/TOCTOU/spawn-binding away.

The dispatch's attack 5, a silent v1→v2 path. REFUTED by full recursive diff, and the roster is unusually clean. 17 top-level paths changed; all 17 are on the declared roster; zero unrostered changes. The converse also holds with no padding at all — every rostered path actually moved, including /date (2026-08-14 → 2026-08-15), which is the roster entry that most often turns out to be decorative. I specifically confirmed the untouched set: /authorityClaim, /purpose, /registerRowQuoted, /tcbTextCarriedVerbatim, /taxonomy, /platforms and all five header fields are byte-identical to v1, so nothing was quietly amended under cover of the repair.

That the repair regressed a v1 guarantee — the standard risk when a successor doubles in size. REFUTED. All six of v1's whatThisDoesNotDo denials are retained verbatim, with two added ('Does not QUALIFY G22', 'Does not retarget platform-tcb-contract.v1.json'). reviewGuidance is strictly append-only: v1's eleven-item list is preserved as an exact prefix with nothing dropped. The three substantive refuse entries are unchanged. Only refuse[3]'s parenthetical was lost — ADV-2, and its scope did not widen.

The dispatch's attack 6, SATISFIED / QUALIFIED / implementation. REFUTED by enumerating every occurrence in the bytes. SATISFIED ×2 — one attack instruction, one 'Do not mark DR-126 SATISFIED'. QUALIFIED ×3 — g22.namingStanding 'NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED-NOT-QUALIFIED', g22.doesNotClaim, and one attack instruction. QUALIFY ×3 — all three RESTRICTIVE: 'Does not QUALIFY G22', 'MUST be independently frozen … before G22 can QUALIFY', 'G22 cannot QUALIFY until a signed allowlist carrier exists'. Each of the three makes qualification harder, none asserts it. DEMONSTRATED ×0. 'docs/v2/implementation/' ×2, both denials. Header discipline intact: CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING.

That per-OS tables were populated under cover of the new platformProfile object — the live risk when a successor adds concrete-looking platform rows. REFUTED. slice1Profiles names four os/arch pairs that /platforms/slice1 already contained in v1 (verified equal as sets), plus filesystem values that are explicit deferrals ('…-as-declared-at-qualification'). Not one concrete member appears anywhere: no package name, no vendor, no version string, no digest. memberPopulation and prequalificationAuthorshipBoundary both restate the reservation, and the second draws the authorship line explicitly — 'A later G22 packet that populates members is a different artifact.'

That D-006's numbers were re-decided. REFUTED absolutely and mechanically: v2 contains NO numeric quantities. Zero MB/ms/GB/% tokens across 13535 bytes, and the only multi-digit tokens in the whole file remain '04' and '308' — a filename fragment and a line number, unchanged from v1. The document doubled in size without acquiring a single number.

That the S1 carrier join exports DR-126's authority to DR-101/DR-103, or double-claims it. REFUTED, and verified reciprocal against the live counterpart rather than asserted. tcbCarrier keeps identity policy at DR-126 and assigns only the signed-closure inventory carrier and ceremony elsewhere. Checking the other side of that join in the current distribution-core-inventory-contract.v8: its layerTaxonomy L-TCB entry reads 'identity rules are DR-126's', its graphRules read 'The L-TCB boundary is DR-126's per ID-DEP-K2', and ID-DEP-K2 rides on 'DR-126 / G22'. Each row points at the other for exactly the half it does not hold. No orphan, no overlap.

The artifact records COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at a28f7a23… 'measuredAtHead 9b06a2fe…'. REFUTED by equality test against live: the six TCB lines are byte-identical to file 04 lines 161-166; rowVerbatim is byte-identical to file 08 line 308; '| DR-126 |' still occurs exactly once in the register so the anchor resolves uniquely; both source digests still MATCH live (a74b4511…, 1cdcf9d4…); the eight-class taxonomy is unchanged.

verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 4 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. REJECT.
verdictStatement: Four of the five claimed repairs are sound, and they are better than the findings they answer. The identity rule no longer admits a bare version string and says so twice; byte collections must bind a digest and a membership rule, with the algorithm required to exist but chosen at population time, which constrains without committing fiat. The resolution predicate is total and — I attacked this specifically — fails closed when no qualified profile is active, because an entry keyed to no active profile can match nothing and the closing universal refuses everything else. The trace boundary covers initial image, late loads, spawned helpers and non-loader system-class access, and I could not name a fifth route in; the join clause is what makes it probative, since a partial trace fails rather than passes quietly. The carrier split I verified from both ends: DR-101's live v8 points identity at DR-126 while v2 points the inventory carrier at DR-101/DR-103, each holding exactly the half the other disclaims. The roster is the cleanest I have measured in this corpus — 17 changed paths, 17 rostered, zero escapees and zero padding — the verbatim carries and the eight-class taxonomy are byte-identical to v1 and to live, and the document more than doubled in size without acquiring a single number, so D-006 remains untouchable from here. My own four v1 advisories were all folded, including the re-measurement block, which now names the HEAD it was taken at and proved exactly correct at that HEAD when I resolved an apparent mismatch to D-108 landing mid-review. What fails is the first repair's own worked example. The artifact authors a four-component profile key, binds it to every allowlist entry with the strictest admission rule in the document — 'An entry without a profile key is a failed successor' — and then ships four slice-1 profiles that each carry three of the four. supportedVersionOrBuildSelector appears exactly once in 13535 bytes, in the key list, and nowhere else: not instantiated, not deferred, not routed to an owner. That it is an oversight rather than a reservation is settled by the sibling component in the same objects, where the deferral is written into the value as 'as-declared-at-qualification' — the drafter had the idiom and applied it once. The cost is concrete: as written, two macOS releases on arm64 are one profile, so an allowlist entry spans system libraries whose identities genuinely differ, which is the drift NT-TCB-3 exists to refuse.
